This week's story
Dot
and
the
Egg
in
the
Grass
An
original
Jurassic
English
story
Dot was a small green dinosaur. She liked to walk by the river every morning.
One morning, Dot stopped. In the long grass, there was an egg. It was round and white, with little brown spots.
"Hello, egg," said Dot. "Who do you belong to?"
The egg did not answer. Eggs never do.
Dot looked up. A bird sat in a tall tree. "Is this your egg?" asked Dot.
The bird looked down. "No," said the bird. "My eggs are blue. And they are up here, in my nest."
Dot thought. "This egg is not blue. And it is not in a tree. So it is not a bird's egg."
Next, Dot saw a big brown dinosaur. "Is this your egg?"
The big dinosaur laughed. "No! My eggs are as big as you, Dot. That egg is too small."
Dot looked at the egg again. It was small. It was round. It was near the water.
Then Dot saw something on the sand. Little tracks went from the river to the grass and back again.
Dot followed the tracks. At the end, by the water, sat a turtle.
"Is this your egg?" asked Dot.
The turtle smiled. "Yes! I put my eggs near the river, in the warm grass. Thank you for keeping it safe."
Dot smiled too. "I didn't know whose egg it was," she said. "But the clues told me."
